complaint.preset.1: Slept through the meeting, snoring included.
complaint.preset.2: Finished the coffee and never made more. Unforgivable.
complaint.preset.3: Dumped all the work on me, then rewarded themselves.
complaint.preset.4: Promised on the phone, then simply backed out.
complaint.preset.5: Gets way too creative with the numbers.
complaint.preset.6: Ate my lunch from the fridge. It had my name on it.
complaint.preset.7: Keeps saying "I have a meeting" and vanishing.
mail.template.0: Hi, let us finish the task today and talk it over at the meeting.
mail.template.0.title: Reminder
mail.template.1: Thanks for the help. I owe you a coffee.
mail.template.1.title: Thanks
mail.template.2: I am sharing my numbers; if you share yours we all come out fine.
mail.template.2.title: Teaming up
mail.template.3: Careful, I think someone is up to something.
mail.template.3.title: Heads up
mail.template.4: Could you do me a favour? I will make it worth your while.
mail.template.4.title: Request
mail.template.5: I was too harsh yesterday, sorry. Let us focus on the work.
mail.template.5.title: Apology
mail.template.6: Send some money and I will back you. Promise.
mail.template.6.title: Offer
mail.template.7: Your numbers look great. Even if half of them are true.
mail.template.7.title: Teasing
task.archive_visitor.fact.capacity: The visitor can fetch at most {n1} documents
task.archive_visitor.fact.hr_file: Document {i1} is an HR file about: {p}
task.archive_visitor.name: Archive Visitor
task.archive_visitor.rule: One person holds today's visitor badge and can fetch only a few documents; everyone else needs one.
task.archive_visitor.tut.1.body: Today's visitor can fetch only a few documents from the archive. Everyone else is waiting for one.
task.archive_visitor.tut.1.example: The visitor fetches 3 documents, 4 people are waiting: one is left out.
task.archive_visitor.tut.1.title: The goal
task.archive_visitor.tut.2.body: Requesters see the document they need. The visitor sees all six documents and one HR file.
task.archive_visitor.tut.2.title: Your information
task.archive_visitor.tut.3.body: The visitor can be busy: text if the line is taken. As a requester, name your document; as the visitor, ask who needs what.
task.archive_visitor.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.archive_visitor.tut.4.body: The visitor ticks the documents to fetch (limited). A requester confirms the document they need. Then submit.
task.archive_visitor.tut.4.example: The visitor picked 3 documents; the requester confirmed "Raise requests".
task.archive_visitor.tut.4.title: What to do
task.archive_visitor.tut.5.body: A requester whose document was fetched and who confirmed it is served. Copying the HR file is sabotage: it lowers the score, reveals one colleague's objective category and leaves a badge-log record.
task.archive_visitor.tut.5.title: What it means
task.bonus_pool.control.choice: How do you split the bonus?
task.bonus_pool.name: Client Bonus Pool
task.bonus_pool.rule: Secretly Share or Take everything: greed costs the client relationship.
task.bonus_pool.tut.1.body: Secretly choose Share or Take everything. If you both share, things go well.
task.bonus_pool.tut.1.example: You both share: the company gets full score.
task.bonus_pool.tut.1.title: The goal
task.bonus_pool.tut.2.body: The only thing you know in this task: who your partner is.
task.bonus_pool.tut.2.title: Your information
task.bonus_pool.tut.3.body: Talk: make promises, or bluff. Afterwards your partner will see your choice, and you theirs.
task.bonus_pool.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.bonus_pool.tut.4.body: Make your choice and submit. You can change it until time runs out.
task.bonus_pool.tut.4.title: What to do
task.bonus_pool.tut.5.body: Both sharing is the best result. If one takes, the taker gains but the company loses. If both take, everyone loses. Taking is not sabotage, but your partner will remember it.
task.bonus_pool.tut.5.example: One takes, one shares: the taker gets +5 money, the company 60.
task.bonus_pool.tut.5.title: What it means
task.budget_split.control.request: How many units do you ask for?
task.budget_split.name: Department Budget
task.budget_split.rule: There is one shared budget: ask for what you need, and if the requests overflow, everyone gets cut.
task.budget_split.tut.1.body: Every project draws on one shared budget. The goal: stay inside it so every project can run.
task.budget_split.tut.1.example: Budget 10, four people: needs of 2, 2, 3, 3. Everyone asking exactly fits.
task.budget_split.tut.1.title: The goal
task.budget_split.tut.2.body: Only you know your own need. The budget and head count are public.
task.budget_split.tut.2.title: Your information
task.budget_split.tut.3.body: Talk to anyone: who asks for what, who has slack? It will come up in the meeting too.
task.budget_split.tut.3.example: "I'll ask for 3, you?" If the total tops the budget we all get trimmed.
task.budget_split.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.budget_split.tut.4.body: Key in how many units you ask for and submit. You can change it until time runs out.
task.budget_split.tut.4.title: What to do
task.budget_split.tut.5.body: If the requests overflow, every grant is cut proportionally, and a project below its need fails. Asking for extra pays off, but puts everyone at risk.
task.budget_split.tut.5.example: If everyone asks for 4 the budget overflows and nobody gets enough.
task.budget_split.tut.5.title: What it means
task.customer_spec.fact.commission: Secret commission: you get a side payment if {i1} is ordered.
task.customer_spec.name: Customer Spec
task.customer_spec.rule: The customer's wishes are split between you: order the one product that matches all of them.
task.customer_spec.tut.1.body: The customer wants three things: colour, size, delivery day. Order the one model out of six that fits all three.
task.customer_spec.tut.1.title: The goal
task.customer_spec.tut.2.body: You see only some of the customer's wishes; your partner sees the rest. The catalogue is public.
task.customer_spec.tut.2.example: You: red, large. Your partner: Tuesday.
task.customer_spec.tut.2.title: Your information
task.customer_spec.tut.3.body: Talk to your partner: say which wish you see, learn theirs.
task.customer_spec.tut.3.example: "I know colour and size: red, large. What is the day?"
task.customer_spec.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.customer_spec.tut.4.body: Find the model that fits all three wishes, pick it and submit. Some decoys fit only two.
task.customer_spec.tut.4.example: Red · large · Tuesday = model 2. Pick that.
task.customer_spec.tut.4.title: What to do
task.customer_spec.tut.5.body: A correct order earns company points. The model with your secret commission is usually the wrong one: your gain and your partner's work can clash.
task.customer_spec.tut.5.example: Wrong model: that group scores nothing.
task.customer_spec.tut.5.title: What it means
task.invoice_reconcile.fact.groups_corre: Groups that got it fully right: {n1}/{n2}
task.invoice_reconcile.fact.partner: The other half of the invoice: {p}
task.invoice_reconcile.name: Invoice Reconciliation
task.invoice_reconcile.rule: You and your partner each hold half of an invoice: both of you must enter the exact total.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.1.body: Add up every line of the invoice and enter the exact total. You hold half, your partner holds half.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.1.example: You have 7 and 4, your partner has 9 and 3. Total: 23.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.1.title: The goal
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.2.body: You only see your own two lines. Your partner's lines are not on your screen.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.2.title: Your information
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.3.body: Your partner is listed on the left. Call or text: ask for their lines, tell them yours.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.3.example: "Mine are 7 and 4, yours?" Or send it in writing.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.4.body: Add the four lines, key in the total and submit. You can fix it until time runs out.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.4.title: What to do
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.5.body: Correct entries earn the company points. Padding the invoice is sabotage: it pays extra, lowers the group's score and leaves a bank record.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.5.example: A wrong total scores nothing. Padding drags the group score down too.
task.invoice_reconcile.tut.5.title: What it means
task.phishing_check.fact.account: Last 4 digits of the account in your email: {acct}
task.phishing_check.fact.insider_offer: Insider offer: the fake account is {acct}; +{n2} money if the payment goes through.
task.phishing_check.name: Suspicious Payment
task.phishing_check.rule: One of you received the supplier email with a fake bank account: flag whose mailbox it is before the payment runs.
task.phishing_check.tut.1.body: One mailbox received an email with a fake account number. Find whose it is before the payment runs.
task.phishing_check.tut.1.example: Flag the right person and the payment stops.
task.phishing_check.tut.1.title: The goal
task.phishing_check.tut.2.body: You see the last four digits of the account in your email. The fake one will differ.
task.phishing_check.tut.2.title: Your information
task.phishing_check.tut.3.body: Compare account numbers with everyone: whose differs from the rest?
task.phishing_check.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.phishing_check.tut.4.body: Flag a mailbox (it can be your own) and submit.
task.phishing_check.tut.4.title: What to do
task.phishing_check.tut.5.body: If the most-flagged person is right the payment stops for full score; otherwise very little. The insider offer is sabotage: pays if the payment goes through, leaves a bank record.
task.phishing_check.tut.5.example: On a tie nobody counts as flagged.
task.phishing_check.tut.5.title: What it means
task.report_review.control.decision: Decision on the report you approve
task.report_review.fact.audit_figure: You hold the true figure of {p}'s report: {n1}
task.report_review.fact.my_figure: Your true figure: {n1} · the polished one: {n2}
task.report_review.group.0: Author of the report you approve
task.report_review.name: Report Review
task.report_review.rule: You write one report and approve another; a third colleague holds the true figure of the report you approve.
task.report_review.tut.1.body: You write a report and approve someone else's. A third person holds the true figure of the report you approve.
task.report_review.tut.1.example: You approve A; A's true figure sits with C.
task.report_review.tut.1.title: The goal
task.report_review.tut.2.body: You see your true figure and its "polished" version. The figure of the report you approve shows once its author submits.
task.report_review.tut.2.title: Your information
task.report_review.tut.3.body: Ask the author of the report you approve, and whoever holds its true figure: does the number add up? Ask before you decide.
task.report_review.tut.3.example: "Yours says 48, mine says 64; which one is right?"
task.report_review.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.report_review.tut.4.body: First pick your own report version (it locks on submit). Once its author has submitted, approve or reject.
task.report_review.tut.4.example: I wrote the true figure. Now approve or reject.
task.report_review.tut.4.title: What to do
task.report_review.tut.5.body: An accurate report that is approved scores full points; a polished one that is approved scores little. Polishing is sabotage: it may pay the author extra but leaves a draft-history trail.
task.report_review.tut.5.example: Accurate + approve = full score. Polished + approve = low score.
task.report_review.tut.5.title: What it means
task.room_booking.fact.ok_slot: A slot that works for you: {slot}
task.room_booking.name: Meeting Room
task.room_booking.rule: There is one slot fewer than people: book one that works for you; two bookings on the same slot cancel both.
task.room_booking.tut.1.body: There is one slot fewer than people. Everyone picks a slot that works; avoid collisions.
task.room_booking.tut.1.example: 4 people, 3 slots: someone has to yield.
task.room_booking.tut.1.title: The goal
task.room_booking.tut.2.body: You see your client's value and the two slots that suit you. Which slots exist is public.
task.room_booking.tut.2.title: Your information
task.room_booking.tut.3.body: Talk to everyone: who takes which slot? If the lowest-value client yields, everybody wins.
task.room_booking.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.room_booking.tut.4.body: Pick a slot or yield, then submit. You can change it until time runs out.
task.room_booking.tut.4.title: What to do
task.room_booking.tut.5.body: A slot booked by exactly one person who accepts it succeeds. Two bookings on one slot are both lost. Yielding earns a little goodwill.
task.room_booking.tut.5.title: What it means
task.server_code.fact.offer: A competitor's offer: +{n1} money if the maintenance fails.
task.server_code.name: Server Maintenance Code
task.server_code.rule: Everyone holds one digit of the maintenance code: more than half of you must enter the exact code.
task.server_code.tut.1.body: Each person holds one digit of the code. If more than half enter it exactly, the maintenance runs.
task.server_code.tut.1.example: 5 digits: at least 3 people must get it right.
task.server_code.tut.1.title: The goal
task.server_code.tut.2.body: You see your own digit's position and value, plus the next digit. Who owns which position is public.
task.server_code.tut.2.title: Your information
task.server_code.tut.3.body: Talk to everyone and put the digits together. One person knows only two digits.
task.server_code.tut.3.example: "Position 2 is 7, position 3 is 1; what is position 1?"
task.server_code.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.server_code.tut.4.body: Key in the whole code and submit. The digit count has to be exact.
task.server_code.tut.4.title: What to do
task.server_code.tut.5.body: If most get it right the company scores full; otherwise only part. The competitor's offer is sabotage: it pays you if the maintenance fails, and leaves a bank record.
task.server_code.tut.5.title: What it means
task.shift_cover.name: Weekend Shifts
task.shift_cover.rule: Weekend shifts must be covered: volunteers get overtime, free riders get the weekend.
task.shift_cover.tut.1.body: Weekend shifts have to be covered. Volunteers earn overtime, free riders keep their weekend.
task.shift_cover.tut.1.example: 3 shifts, 5 people: at least 3 volunteers are needed.
task.shift_cover.tut.1.title: The goal
task.shift_cover.tut.2.body: You see which shifts you can take and what volunteering costs you. How many shifts exist is public.
task.shift_cover.tut.2.title: Your information
task.shift_cover.tut.3.body: Talk: who takes which shift? Two people on one shift is a waste.
task.shift_cover.tut.3.example: "I will take Sunday, can you do Saturday evening?"
task.shift_cover.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.shift_cover.tut.4.body: Pick a shift or say not this weekend, then submit.
task.shift_cover.tut.4.title: What to do
task.shift_cover.tut.5.body: Every covered shift raises the output and pays the volunteer overtime. If nobody steps up, everyone loses.
task.shift_cover.tut.5.title: What it means
task.supply_swap.fact.collector: Collector bonus: a payout if you still hold {item} at the end.
task.supply_swap.name: Supply Swap
task.supply_swap.rule: Your project needs two items you do not have: trade with your colleagues.
task.supply_swap.tut.1.body: Your project needs two items; you hold other ones. Trade so that everyone's project gets done.
task.supply_swap.tut.1.example: You need a stapler, you hold a power strip.
task.supply_swap.tut.1.title: The goal
task.supply_swap.tut.2.body: You see what you need, what you hold, and one "collector" item.
task.supply_swap.tut.2.example: Need: Stapler, Mug. Holding: Power strip, Paper clips.
task.supply_swap.tut.2.title: Your information
task.supply_swap.tut.3.body: Everyone holds someone else's need. Who has yours? Ask and tell.
task.supply_swap.tut.3.example: "Who has a stapler? I have a power strip."
task.supply_swap.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.supply_swap.tut.4.body: Click a person's name to give them an item. Say you are done when you are.
task.supply_swap.tut.4.title: What to do
task.supply_swap.tut.5.body: Every completed project earns company points. Keeping the collector item pays a little extra but breaks someone else's project.
task.supply_swap.tut.5.title: What it means
task.vendor_pick.fact.kickback: The weak vendor ({vendor}) pays you +{n2} money if it wins.
task.vendor_pick.name: Vendor Selection
task.vendor_pick.rule: Each of you tested one vendor: vote for the best, and the winner's quality is the company's result.
task.vendor_pick.tut.1.body: Each of you tested a different vendor. If the best one wins, the company wins.
task.vendor_pick.tut.1.example: Qualities 3, 5, 7, 9: the winner's quality sets the result.
task.vendor_pick.tut.1.title: The goal
task.vendor_pick.tut.2.body: You only know the quality of the vendor you tested. Others tested other vendors.
task.vendor_pick.tut.2.title: Your information
task.vendor_pick.tut.3.body: Talk: put everyone's qualities together and find the best.
task.vendor_pick.tut.3.title: Who to contact
task.vendor_pick.tut.4.body: Vote for a vendor and submit.
task.vendor_pick.tut.4.title: What to do
task.vendor_pick.tut.5.body: The most-voted vendor wins and the output follows its quality. The weak vendor's offer is sabotage: it pays you if it wins, and leaves a bank record.
task.vendor_pick.tut.5.title: What it means
